jobs.description: Skip to content Live Demo Your AI Agents are Acting Now...Are You in Control? How to secure agent access across MCP & AI frameworks (AWS, Claude, OpenAI) Sep 16, 2026 / 12PM ET | 4PM GMT AI agents are accessing enterprise systems in different ways, from AI applications querying internal databases, to AI assistants logging into password-based business apps, coding agents accessing production infrastructure, and business assistants connecting to SaaS through MCP. Each use case introduces a different mix of credential exposure and activity risk, and requires the right controls for how the agent accesses systems and what it is allowed to do. Join our live demo, featuring leading cybersecurity analyst Paul Webber from Software Analyst Cyber Research [SACR], to see how organizations are preparing to secure AI agent access at runtime and how Akeyless Agentic Runtime Authority addresses these risks. SecretlessAI™ keeps credentials out of the agent, while Runtime Authority constrains the agent to the authority appropriate for the task and applies intent-aware controls to allow, filter, mask, or block actions at runtime, with complete traceability from identity and prompt to action and outcome. You’ll see runtime protection across MCP and leading AI platforms and frameworks, including AWS, OpenAI, and Claude, from a coding agent accessing production to an autonomous agent acting across enterprise systems. What we will cover in the demo: A coding agent connecting to production SecretlessAI™ brokering access without exposing credentials to the agent The agent attempting a risky action Runtime Authority blocking it in real time A full audit trail from prompt to action Speakers Yael Fainaro Chief Strategy Officer, Akeyless Paul Webber Principal Cybersecurity Analyst, SACR Vani Thiruvengadam Director Solutions Engineering, Akeyless We use cookies and similar technologies, to enhance your experience on the website, analyze site usage and performance, such cookies access and store information from your browser and device. AI Agents Break Traditional Identity Security AI agents operate with too much power and too little oversight. Your coding agent may hold standing keys to production, or find ones you never gave it, sitting in a config file or memory store. Your customer service agent might pull records a human in the role can't and shouldn't. Traditional access control cannot determine intent or keep up with agents acting autonomously in milliseconds. By the time they detect misuse, the damage is done. This Isn't a Future Problem 42% of organizations hardcode AI agent credentials directly in workflows* 81% YoY growth in leaked AI-service credentials on GitHub** 24,000+ secrets exposed in MCP config files in 2025** In 9 Seconds an AI coding agent found an over-privileged credential and deleted a production database*** Full Control, from Credential to Action to Audit. Go Secretless Remove standing credentials entirely with Akeyless SecretlessAI®. Akeyless brokers access through the Gateway and generates scoped, short-lived access for each task across SaaS, web apps, and infrastructure alike. AI agents never receive a secret—no storage, no privilege buildup, and nothing for a compromised or prompt-injected agent to steal. Secure Every Mode of Access Not every agent can go fully secretless. Some still need direct credentials: passwords, API keys, certificates, cryptographic keys. Akeyless governs their issuance, rotation, and revocation under centralized policy, so nothing goes unmanaged or forgotten. Enforce Intent-Aware Policy at Runtime Assess the semantic intent behind each request and constrain the agent to the authority appropriate for the task—even when the underlying user or identity has broader permissions. Enforce policy at runtime to block unauthorized actions and filter or mask sensitive output. Any session can be shut down instantly with a real-time kill switch. Find and Fix What's Exploitable Discover orphaned credentials, stale tokens, and overbroad access that agents could exploit. Identify and prioritize the ones with real potential for harm, and route them to remediation. Trace Actions End-to-End Eliminate the AI black box. Log every credential use and every action, and trace each one back to the human, machine, or agent behind it. One complete audit trail, spanning both credential access and activity.
